answers.children: Yes — Sussex Spaniels are good with children thanks to their gentle and affectionate nature combined with a low-slung sturdy build that tolerates energetic play without being overwhelmed. Their determined hunting background gives them a patient endurance around small children who may tug or chase, though the breed’s stubborn streak can surface if play becomes too rough. The compact size of 35-45 lb makes them an approachable height for family interaction. (PawLabs child-friendly score: 7/10)
answers.other-pets: Yes — Sussex Spaniels generally get along with other pets because their gentle temperament and loyal companion qualities promote peaceful household living. Their excellent scenting ability can trigger focused tracking of smaller animals yet the low prey drive from flushing game rather than pursuing it limits chasing. Same-sex tension remains minimal when properly introduced.
answers.exercise: Sussex Spaniels need 45-60 minutes of daily exercise split into two sessions of steady walking or rambling through fields and wooded areas. Without this their prone-to-weight-gain build turns them into sedentary dogs that gain pounds quickly. Their low-to-the-ground frame and endurance from pushing through dense English underbrush suit methodical scent work and unhurried hikes far better than sprinting.
answers.shedding: Yes — Sussex Spaniels shed moderately year-round with some increase during seasonal coat changes. Their medium double coat of dense undercoat and longer outer layer in the distinctive golden-liver colour traps loose hair that works its way into furniture and clothing. The texture requires regular attention to prevent matting on the low-slung body.
answers.hypoallergenic: No breed is truly hypoallergenic and the Sussex Spaniel is not one of those commonly suggested for allergy sufferers. Its medium double coat produces dander and sheds moderately which spreads allergens around the home. The dense undercoat and longer outer layer developed for flushing game in wet Sussex terrain hold onto dirt and hair that affect sensitive individuals.
answers.training: Sussex Spaniels are not the easiest to train because their determined and stubborn nature can lead to selective listening especially when a scent distracts them during sessions. Bred for methodical flushing and retrieving in thick English cover their independent streak means they were developed to work with minimal direction which reduces biddability. Their intelligence of 7 out of 10 allows progress with patient consistent methods that channel their loyal affectionate side.
answers.lifespan: Sussex Spaniels live 11-13 years. Their health robustness is challenged by a build prone to weight gain that can strain their low-slung frame originally developed for endurance in muddy terrain rather than speed. The affectionate gentle temperament does not alter the moderate lifespan tied to maintaining lean condition and activity levels suited to their sporting origins.
answers.size: Sussex Spaniels reach 35-45 lb and stand 13-15 in at the shoulder. Their low-to-the-ground substantial build with short legs and sturdy proportions feels compact yet solid to live with allowing them to navigate tight spaces while still providing a comforting weight when they lean affectionately against an owner. The medium size suits their role pushing through dense cover without snagging.
answers.barking: Sussex Spaniels do not bark excessively but they produce a characteristic bell-like sound when alerting to game or interesting scents. Their history of flushing game from thick Sussex underbrush led to this deliberate vocalisation that carries through dense cover to guide hunters rather than constant noise. The moderate barking level of 5 out of 10 fits their quiet intensity indoors once exercised.
answers.apartment: Yes — Sussex Spaniels can live in an apartment provided they receive their required daily walks and mental stimulation to prevent boredom from their scent-driven nature. Their gentle affectionate temperament helps them settle calmly indoors after activity and their moderate energy combined with low barking supports neighbour-friendly quietness. The compact low-slung build occupies little space yet their prone-to-weight-gain tendency demands owners prevent couch-potato habits.
answers.first-time: No — Sussex Spaniels are not ideal as a first dog because their stubborn streak during training and determined independent nature demand an experienced handler who can channel their intelligence without frustration. The need to manage their prone-to-weight-gain build alongside consistent exercise and grooming of the medium double coat adds layers of responsibility that challenge novices despite the loyal affectionate rewards.
